screens.title: SIGN IN
screens.note: Email and password, the route to account creation, and the route to password recovery. The RN app has no such screen: sign-in there is Auth0 Universal Login opened in a system browser against https://auth.fluent.pet/authorize, so there is nothing to port.

screens.title: CREATE ACCOUNT
screens.note: Email and one password field with a reveal toggle and a live requirement list. Leads to VERIFY_EMAIL.

screens.title: RESET PASSWORD
screens.note: One email field. Asks for the reset mail to be sent; leads to CHECK_YOUR_EMAIL.

screens.title: CHECK YOUR EMAIL
screens.note: Confirmation that a reset link was sent, with a rate-limited resend. Never claims the address exists — only the mail server knows that.

screens.title: NEW PASSWORD
screens.note: Where the emailed reset link lands. Takes the address and the link's token as query parameters, so the deep link is the whole entry point.

screens.title: VERIFY EMAIL
screens.note: Where sign-up lands: waiting for the verification link to be opened, and the confirmed state the link returns to.

annotations.title: Three names for one concept
annotations.body: The filtered view over Activities is called Dashboard in the route enum, Activity in the tab bar, and its neighbouring screen is called Log. CONTEXT.md keeps all three deliberately; the Flutter rewrite inherits all three.
evidence: Navigator.ACTIVITY = "ActivityNav" — TabBar.tsx labels tabs with route.name.replace("Nav", ""), so the tab reads "Activity"
Screen.LOG = "Log", a separate screen in ModalNavigator

annotations.title: Enum name and route value disagree
annotations.body: Screen.SETTINGS resolves to the route name "Tools", the header reads ADVANCED TOOLS, and the implementation lives in src/Home/Settings. Three names for one drawer destination.

annotations.title: Base section is called Hardware in the UI
annotations.body: The Base tab's navigator is HardwareNav and its header reads HARDWARE, while the domain term in CONTEXT.md is Base. Kept as-is by the plan, but the rewrite has to pick which name each surface shows.
evidence: TabBar.tsx renders route.name.replace("Nav", "") — the tab label is "Hardware"

annotations.title: Route value is a display string
annotations.body: Every other member of the Screen enum is a PascalCase route identifier. These use the human-readable title as the route name, which is also what appears in the deep-link config and in navigation state.

annotations.title: Route value drops the distinguishing word
annotations.body: LOG_DETAILS_EDIT_PUSHER resolves to "LogDetailsEdit", not "LogDetailsEditPusher". Its sibling is "LogDetailsEditButtons", so the two route names differ by a suffix that is present on one and absent on the other.

annotations.title: One component, several route names
annotations.body: These editors are registered more than once so that the LogDetails and LogEntryEdit stacks each get their own route. Same screen, four names — the rewrite needs one widget, not four.

annotations.title: Declared but never registered
annotations.body: Present in the Screen enum but attached to no navigator, so it cannot be navigated to. Nothing to rebuild — listed so the count reconciles.
evidence: Screen.UNKNOWN = "Unknown" — no <Stack.Screen>, <Tab.Screen> or <Drawer.Screen> registration, no deep link

annotations.title: Below the //alpha comment but not part of the learning product
annotations.body: These sit under the //alpha comment in Screen.ts, which would suggest they are retired with the rest of it. They are not: they are registered in ModalNavigator with no isAlpha guard and implemented under Settings. Kept in scope.

annotations.title: Retired despite sitting outside the //alpha block
annotations.body: Grouped with the device-management screens in Screen.ts, but its only registration is behind the isAlpha flag and it renders a learning-product component.
evidence: Screen.LANDING = "Landing" — Registered in LandingNavigator.tsx, which is reachable only behind the isAlpha flag.

annotations.title: Tab bar is three tabs after the scope cut
annotations.body: TabNavigator registers five tabs when isAlpha is on and three when it is off; TabBar.tsx hardcodes the matching widths. With the learning product retired, the tab bar is permanently Household / Activity / Hardware.
evidence: TabNavigator.tsx: LANDING_NAV and MODULE_NAV are inside an `isAlpha ? … : null` branch

annotations.title: Designed for the Flutter app, absent from the RN app
annotations.body: The RN app has no login or signup screen: AuthenticationNavigator.tsx registers WELCOME and nothing else, and sign-in is Auth0 Universal Login opened in a system browser. These screens are native replacements, designed rather than ported. They are the only entries in this map that were not read out of the RN source, they carry invented: true, and they are excluded from the in-scope/retired arithmetic above.
